finding_label: Fermentable substrate responses depend on preparation and community
finding_summary: Resistant starch and pectic substrates can supply microbial SCFA-production capacity; observed responses depend on preparation and community, while the FOS/GOS mixture admission requires review.
finding_statement: Resistant starch and pectic substrates can supply microbial SCFA-production capacity; observed responses depend on preparation and community, while the FOS/GOS mixture admission requires review.
finding_interpretation: Class-level substrate utilisation is distinct from formulation-specific intervention effects. Faecal or luminal concentrations, indirect production estimates and separately infused SCFA handling are not interchangeable measures of substrate-to-product flux.
synthesis: Class-level substrate utilisation is distinct from formulation-specific intervention effects. Faecal or luminal concentrations, indirect production estimates and separately infused SCFA handling are not interchangeable measures of substrate-to-product flux.
synthesis_limitations: No uniform food-specific butyrate response, intake target or brain benefit is established. Secondary synthesis is not independent primary replication; FOS/GOS evidence remains mixture- and sampling-specific.

evidence_considered.label: van Trijp et al. (2024)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Little or no distal-ileal substrate degradation or local SCFA production was detected. One proximal-colonic participant showed increased unlabelled SCFA concentrations after the bolus. Separately infused labelled SCFAs traced product handling; they do not directly measure FOS/GOS-to-SCFA conversion.
evidence_considered.study_exposure: Exploratory human FOS/GOS mixture bolus studies with intestinal sampling and separately infused labelled SCFAs; acute and seven-day intervention contexts.
evidence_considered.study_finding: Little or no distal-ileal substrate degradation or local SCFA production was detected. One proximal-colonic participant showed increased unlabelled SCFA concentrations after the bolus. Separately infused labelled SCFAs traced product handling; they do not directly measure FOS/GOS-to-SCFA conversion.

assessment.study: Exploratory human FOS/GOS mixture bolus studies with intestinal sampling and separately infused labelled SCFAs; acute and seven-day intervention contexts.
assessment.population: Healthy males; sampled sites included distal ileum (n=6), proximal colon (n=1) and transverse/descending colon (n=1).
assessment.result: Little or no distal-ileal substrate degradation or local SCFA production was detected. One proximal-colonic participant showed increased unlabelled SCFA concentrations after the bolus. Separately infused labelled SCFAs traced product handling; they do not directly measure FOS/GOS-to-SCFA conversion.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No generalisable production rate, dietary dose or clinical effect is established.
assessment.evidence_summary: Little or no distal-ileal substrate degradation or local SCFA production was detected. One proximal-colonic participant showed increased unlabelled SCFA concentrations after the bolus. Separately infused labelled SCFAs traced product handling; they do not directly measure FOS/GOS-to-SCFA conversion.
assessment.limitations: An ileal null does not disprove colonic fermentation. Other colonic sampling was dilution-limited. Breath hydrogen and plasma responses are indirect; isotope-derived production estimates and compartment models are inferred, not direct labelled-substrate flux. Mixture results cannot be assigned to individual constituents or butyrate specifically; no food-equivalence or brain outcome is established.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary full text: study design, site-specific sampling, carbohydrate/SCFA results, separately delivered SCFA tracers, production estimation and modelling limitations.

assessment.study: Primary isolate, co-culture and donor-community experiments with resistant-starch preparations including RS2 and RS3.
assessment.population: Human-colonic bacterial isolates and an experimentally supplemented low-utilisation donor community.
assessment.result: Resistant-starch utilisation differed among organisms; primary degraders enabled substrate access by other community members.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No generalisable production rate, dietary dose or clinical effect is established.
assessment.evidence_summary: Resistant-starch utilisation differed among organisms; primary degraders enabled substrate access by other community members.
assessment.limitations: Supports class-level fermentable-substrate capacity beyond a potato formulation, not uniform use of every RS subtype. Ruminococcus bromii is not itself a butyrate producer; cross-feeding and community context matter. No whole-food or brain effect is established.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary full text and abstract: resistant-starch materials, utilisation, co-culture and donor-community experiments.
